# `m.stocks.financials.income_statements`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Income statements of US public companies, one row per filer and reporting period.

```python
m.stocks.financials.income_statements(symbols=None, *, timeframe=None, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Tickers whose filings to return; leave it out for every filing. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `timeframe` | `dm.Timeframe.ANNUAL`, `QUARTERLY`, or `TRAILING_TWELVE_MONTHS`; leave it out for all three. |  |
| `start` | The first period end date. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last period end date. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | Any field of the rows, such as `"fiscal_year"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"fiscal_year_gte": 2020}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Income Statements (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | Not included |
| Stocks Starter | Not included |
| Stocks Developer | Not included |
| Stocks Advanced | End-of-day, All history |
| Financials & Ratios Expansion | End-of-day, All history |
| Stocks Business | Not included |
| Financials & Ratios Expansion Business | End-of-day, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The ticker the request named that the row lists in `Tickers`: a row that lists several of the named tickers appears once for each, so an article about AAPL and MSFT read for both is listed under each. A request that named one ticker gives it to every row. Null when the call named no ticker, and on a row that lists none of a request's named tickers. | REST |
| `BasicEarningsPerShare` | double | Earnings per share calculated using the weighted average number of basic shares outstanding. For TTM records, recalculated as TTM net income divided by average basic shares outstanding over the four quarters. | REST |
| `BasicSharesOutstanding` | double | Weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period, used in basic EPS calculation. For TTM records, represents the average over the four most recent quarters. | REST |
| `Cik` | String | The company's Central Index Key (CIK), a unique identifier assigned by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). You can look up a company’s CIK using the SEC CIK Lookup tool (https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/cik-lookup). | REST |
| `ConsolidatedNetIncomeLoss` | double | Total net income or loss for the consolidated entity including all subsidiaries. | REST |
| `CostOfRevenue` | double | Direct costs attributable to the production of goods or services sold, also known as cost of goods sold (COGS). | REST |
| `DepreciationDepletionAmortization` | double | Non-cash expenses representing the allocation of asset costs over their useful lives. | REST |
| `DilutedEarningsPerShare` | double | Earnings per share calculated using diluted shares outstanding, including the effect of potentially dilutive securities. For TTM records, recalculated as TTM net income divided by average diluted shares outstanding over the four quarters. | REST |
| `DilutedSharesOutstanding` | double | Weighted average number of shares outstanding including the dilutive effect of stock options, warrants, and convertible securities. For TTM records, represents the average over the four most recent quarters. | REST |
| `DiscontinuedOperations` | double | After-tax results from business segments that have been or will be disposed of. | REST |
| `Ebitda` | double | Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a measure of operating performance. | REST |
| `EquityInAffiliates` | double | The company's share of income or losses from equity method investments in affiliated companies. | REST |
| `ExtraordinaryItems` | double | Unusual and infrequent gains or losses that are both unusual in nature and infrequent in occurrence. | REST |
| `FilingDate` | String | The date of the most recent SEC filing that included this period's data. This is not necessarily the date this period was originally filed. Because SEC filings restate comparative data for prior periods, multiple records can share the same filing_date. For example, an annual 10-K reports three years of results, and a 10-Q includes prior period comparatives. To find the original filing date for a specific 10-K or 10-Q, use the SEC EDGAR filings index endpoint (/stocks/filings/vX/index). | REST |
| `FiscalQuarter` | long | The fiscal quarter number (1, 2, 3, or 4) for the reporting period. | REST |
| `FiscalYear` | long | The fiscal year for the reporting period. | REST |
| `GrossProfit` | double | Revenue minus cost of revenue, representing profit before operating expenses. | REST |
| `IncomeBeforeIncomeTaxes` | double | Pre-tax income calculated as operating income plus total other income/expense. | REST |
| `IncomeTaxes` | double | Income tax expense or benefit for the period. | REST |
| `InterestExpense` | double | Cost of borrowed funds, including interest on debt and other financing obligations. | REST |
| `InterestIncome` | double | Income earned from interest-bearing investments and cash equivalents. | REST |
| `NetIncomeLossAttributableCommonShareholders` | double | Net income or loss available to common shareholders after preferred dividends and noncontrolling interests. | REST |
| `NoncontrollingInterest` | double | The portion of net income attributable to minority shareholders in consolidated subsidiaries. | REST |
| `OperatingIncome` | double | Income from operations calculated as gross profit minus total operating expenses, excluding non-operating items. | REST |
| `OtherIncomeExpense` | double | Non-operating income and expenses not related to the company's core business operations. | REST |
| `OtherOperatingExpenses` | double | Operating expenses not classified in the main expense categories. | REST |
| `PeriodEnd` | String | The last date of the reporting period (formatted as YYYY-MM-DD). | REST |
| `PreferredStockDividendsDeclared` | double | Dividends declared on preferred stock during the period. | REST |
| `ResearchDevelopment` | double | Expenses incurred for research and development activities to create new products or improve existing ones. | REST |
| `Revenue` | double | Total revenue or net sales for the period, representing the company's gross income from operations. | REST |
| `SellingGeneralAdministrative` | double | Expenses related to selling products and general administrative costs not directly tied to production. | REST |
| `Tickers` | String[] | A list of ticker symbols under which the company is listed. Multiple symbols may indicate different share classes for the same company. | REST |
| `Timeframe` | String | The reporting period type. Possible values include: quarterly, annual, trailing_twelve_months. | REST |
| `TotalOperatingExpenses` | double | Sum of all operating expenses including cost of revenue, SG&A, R&D, depreciation, and other operating expenses. | REST |
| `TotalOtherIncomeExpense` | double | Net total of all non-operating income and expenses including interest income, interest expense, and other items. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
